prompt_text: What is the best AI video ad maker?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there’s no one “best” AI video-ad maker — the right choice depends on your use case (talking-head vs. animated/social, single ads vs. large-scale personalized campaigns), budget, and output platform. Below are the top options by common needs and why you might pick each.

Quick recommendations
- Best for AI presenters / talking-head ads: Synthesia or HeyGen
  - Why: realistic AI avatars, many languages/voices, fast script → video. Great for product demos, explainer ads, and multilingual versions without hiring actors.
  - Drawbacks: can feel synthetic for highly emotional creative; cost per minute/licenses.

- Best for quick social ads from templates: Canva or InVideo (now known as InVideo / Vidyo)
  - Why: huge template libraries for Facebook/Instagram/TikTok specs, drag-and-drop, stock video/graphics, basic AI copy/voice features.
  - Drawbacks: less advanced generative features; animations templated.

- Best for repurposing long content into short ads: Pictory, Opus Clip, or Vidyo.ai
  - Why: automatically finds highlights, creates short-form clips with captions optimized for social.
  - Drawbacks: limited creative control vs. manual editing.

- Best for advanced generative visuals / creative flexibility: Runway
  - Why: state-of-the-art text-to-video, generative editing, background/scene changes. Good for standout visual styles.
  - Drawbacks: steeper learning curve, heavier compute cost.

- Best for quick branded promo videos: Promo.com or Biteable
  - Why: marketing-focused templates, licensed music, optimized ad lengths.
  - Drawbacks: less AI-scripting sophistication.

- Best for large-scale personalized video ads (enterprise): Idomoo, SundaySky, or Clinch
  - Why: dynamic personalization at scale (data-driven video variants, ad personalization).
  - Drawbacks: enterprise pricing, integration effort.

How to choose (short checklist)
- Output type: talking-head vs. animated vs. repurposed clips
- Scale: one-off ads vs. hundreds of personalized variants
- Platform: TikTok vertical vs. YouTube widescreen
- Budget: free/cheap vs. subscription vs. enterprise
- Language/voice needs: multi-language TTS and accents?
- Speed vs. control: auto-generated vs. manual/creative polish

Price/tier notes
- Canva, Pictory, InVideo: affordable subscriptions, free tiers with limits.
- Synthesia/HeyGen/Elai: mid-range per-video or subscription; pay more for premium avatars/enterprise.
- Runway: pay-as-you-go credits/tiers, more for heavy generative use.
- Idomoo/SundaySky: enterprise pricing.

Ethics & legal tip
- If using realistic AI faces/voices, disclose synthetic content where appropriate and ensure you have rights for any brand/celebrity likenesses.

If you tell me your budget, target platform (TikTok, Facebook, YouTube), whether you want an AI presenter or animated/video-film look, and whether you need one ad or many personalized versions, I can recommend the single best tool and a step-by-step workflow for producing your ad.
